text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Arab and international press give prominence to President Saddam Hussein's anti-U.S. remarks.
- Food supplies flow to Iraq via its southern ports.
- Egyptian women demonstrate against normalisation of ties with Israel.
- France opposes U.S. control of NATO.
- Tunisian president calls for the lifting of sanctions on Iraq.
- Malaysian and Egyptian companies to hold specialised exhibitions in Iraq.
- Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf arrives in Rabat.
- Iraq calls on Arabs to be self-sufficient in pharmaceutical production.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz receives French delegation.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and QADISSIYA)
- Editorial lambasts United States and U.N. arms envoy Rolf Ekeus for saying Iraq still represented a threat to regional stability.
- Police catch gang of thieves in Wasit, a province in southern Iraq.
- Anti-biotics factory to start production by early April.
- Article urging Kurds to make peace with the central government in Baghdad.
- Article attempts to prove that Iraq emerged victorious in the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
